scope: Primary-source toolkit and research evidence for an educational utility-operator tutorial. Tool capabilities are not evidence of field deployment.
evidence_rules: Use 'current verified examples' rather than claiming an exhaustive list of the latest tools.
Present the proposed utility architecture and scenario as tutorial designs, not vendor deployments.
Separate software capabilities, research evaluations, and demonstrated company deployments.
Pin framework, protocol, benchmark, model, and task versions when reproducing results.

entries.title: LangGraph
entries.verified_capabilities: Mix deterministic checks and LLM decisions in a stateful graph; persist progress, stream execution, and pause for human oversight.
entries.utility_teaching_use: Make alarm triage an explicit graph: retrieve evidence, diagnose, validate, request approval, then record the approved work item.
entries.limitation: Low-level runtime: application authors still implement data access, policies, storage, and validation. It does not certify grid decisions.
entries.date_note: Live documentation reviewed 2026-10-17; no package-version claim.

entries.title: Microsoft Agent Framework
entries.verified_capabilities: Combines agents, workflow graphs, model clients, middleware and MCP. Checkpoints save workflow state and support resumption.
entries.utility_teaching_use: Resume a maintenance investigation after an operator shift change or service restart.
entries.limitation: An in-memory checkpoint does not survive restart. Persistent checkpoints are sensitive trusted state; identities and topology must remain compatible. Go has documented preview limitations.

entries.title: OpenAI Agents SDK and component lifecycle
entries.verified_capabilities: Python/TypeScript agent orchestration with tools, handoffs, guardrails, human review, state and tracing; the application owns deployment and approval decisions.
entries.utility_teaching_use: Wrap approved historian queries, procedure retrieval, and draft work-order creation as narrowly scoped functions.
entries.limitation: Guardrails are application mechanisms, not proof of physical safety. Agent Builder is deprecated, with shutdown scheduled 2026-11-30; ChatKit remains available. The separate Evals platform also has a scheduled 2026-11-30 shutdown.

entries.title: Google Agent Development Kit (ADK) 2.0
entries.verified_capabilities: Adds graph workflows that combine agents, tools and functions; supports structured routing, human input, dynamic workflows, and evaluation of tool trajectories and response quality.
entries.utility_teaching_use: Build a procedure assistant whose deterministic workflow requests missing asset identity before an agent reasons over the evidence.
entries.limitation: Language feature parity and migration details vary. A response-safety score does not measure electrical operating safety.

entries.title: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
entries.verified_capabilities: Standardizes discovery and invocation of tools, resources and prompts between AI applications and external systems.
entries.utility_teaching_use: Place a governed gateway in front of read-only historian, GIS, manuals and asset-registry connectors.
entries.limitation: A protocol does not establish permission or trust by itself. Authenticate users and servers, scope access, validate token audiences, and do not pass downstream tokens through unchanged.

entries.title: Agent2Agent (A2A)
entries.verified_capabilities: Agent Cards describe capabilities; task/message/artifact operations support delegation across separately implemented agents, including streaming and asynchronous work.
entries.utility_teaching_use: Let an operations assistant request a bounded diagnosis from a separately governed asset-health agent.
entries.limitation: A2A handles collaboration; MCP handles tool/context access. Both require authentication and application policy. Protocol conformance does not verify returned engineering advice.
entries.date_note: Current specification reviewed 2026-10-17; its migration section describes v1.0 breaking changes.

entries.title: AIOpsLab
entries.verified_capabilities: Deploys microservice environments, injects faults, generates workloads and telemetry, and exposes an interface to evaluate agents across incident tasks.
entries.utility_teaching_use: Teach detect-diagnose-plan-act-verify in an isolated utility IT or communications-service sandbox before considering an OT pilot.
entries.limitation: This is cloud-operations research; its results are not evidence of safe autonomous switching or generation dispatch.

entries.title: Evaluation toolkit: tau-bench family, AgentDojo, ADK Arena
entries.verified_capabilities: tau²-bench tests agent/user coordination in telecom; AgentDojo tests prompt injection in tool-returned data; ADK Arena compares frameworks with a fixed LLM developer.
entries.utility_teaching_use: Measure repeated success, policy compliance, operator coordination, attack resistance, cost and recovery on local scenarios.
entries.limitation: Benchmarks are proxies, not certification. Simulator choice, task revisions and harness configuration change scores; ADK Arena is a work-in-progress preprint.
entries.date_note: tau² paper 2025-06-09; AgentDojo revised 2024-11-24; ADK Arena submitted 2026-06-04; tau repository includes 2026 updates.

research_lessons.title: Evaluate coordinated action, not fluent answers
research_lessons.evidence: tau²-bench gives both the agent and simulated user tools in a shared telecom environment, exposing reasoning and coordination failures.
research_lessons.teaching_inference: For operators, grade whether the assistant requests the right evidence, communicates a clear next step, and reaches the allowed final state. Repeat each case; one successful run is insufficient.

research_lessons.title: Treat retrieved content as evidence with a trust boundary
research_lessons.evidence: AgentDojo studies malicious instructions embedded in tool results and evaluates both legitimate task completion and attacker goals.
research_lessons.teaching_inference: A maintenance PDF, alarm annotation or vendor response must not grant tool permissions. Put authorization and action validation outside the model.

research_lessons.title: Select the complete system through local evaluation
research_lessons.evidence: ADK Arena's June 2026 preprint compares 51 Python frameworks and finds no framework dominates across its tested benchmarks.
research_lessons.teaching_inference: Choose on your tasks, access controls, maintainability, latency and evidence quality; avoid equating a framework logo or leaderboard rank with utility readiness.

suggested_utility_architecture.status: Proposed educational architecture; not a claim about any named utility.
suggested_utility_architecture.use_case: Transformer cooling alarm: gather evidence and draft a maintenance work order for an operator.

flow.label: Read-only event input
flow.detail: An event bus supplies alarm ID, asset ID and timestamp from a historian/EMS/ADMS mirror. Validate timestamp, asset mapping and data freshness.

flow.label: Governed evidence tools
flow.detail: Use scoped APIs or MCP for trends, asset registry, current procedures, weather and maintenance history. Preserve source IDs and timestamps.

flow.label: Bounded orchestration
flow.detail: A durable graph routes retrieval and analysis. A single agent can own the workflow; add specialists or A2A only where separate ownership helps.

flow.label: Deterministic validation
flow.detail: Check units, missing signals, procedure revision, action allowlist and tool arguments. Invoke approved engineering calculators or simulators for numerical work.

flow.label: Operator review
flow.detail: Show evidence, uncertainty and proposed action. Stop and escalate when evidence conflicts or required data is absent.

flow.label: Controlled business action
flow.detail: After authenticated approval, a separate service may create a draft work item with an idempotency key. Re-read the record and log the result.

continuous_controls: Separate the reasoning service from control-plane credentials; keep protection and real-time control in existing deterministic systems.
Least privilege, per-tool scopes, immutable audit trail, protected checkpoint storage, budget and timeout limits.
Capture model/framework/tool versions, retrieved evidence, operator decision, tool outcome and recovery path.
Evaluate in replay/shadow mode first, then stage a narrowly scoped pilot using site-approved acceptance criteria.
metrics: Task completion with correct final state
suggested_utility_architecture.inference_note: Architecture and acceptance suggestions are an educational synthesis, not directly prescribed or certified by these sources.
